name: Non-syndromic Non-specific Multisutural Craniosynostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Multisutural Craniosynostosis

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal skull shape due to premature fusion of two or more cranial sutures without associated syndromic features
CT scan or 3D imaging demonstrating premature fusion of multiple cranial sutures
Absence of clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic craniosynostosis (e.g., no FGFR mutations or associated anomalies)
No significant developmental delay or neurological deficits at diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Premature fusion of multiple cranial sutures confirmed by imaging, with absence of syndromic features and typical clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical, radiological, and genetic assessment to exclude syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Premature fusion of multiple cranial sutures
searchTerms: early fusion of multiple skull bones

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal skull morphology with multisutural involvement
pathognomonic.notes: Includes brachycephaly, plagiocephaly, or complex skull shape
searchTerms: skull shape abnormal with multiple fused sutures

common.notes: May present as irritability or vomiting
searchTerms: headache and vomiting from brain swelling

common.notes: May be noted on physical exam
searchTerms: slow closing of soft spot on head

occasional.notes: Due to orbital involvement or increased intracranial pressure
May develop secondary to impaired CSF flow

rare.symptomName: Respiratory difficulties due to midface hypoplasia
searchTerms: respiratory difficulty due to small midface
airway issues from facial bone hypoplasia
fluid buildup in brain needing shunting

laboratory: Genetic testing negative for syndromic craniosynostosis mutations (e.g., FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3, TWIST1)
imaging: CT scan with 3D reconstruction showing premature fusion of multiple cranial sutures
MRI to assess brain structure and rule out associated anomalies
other: Clinical evaluation excluding syndromic features such as limb anomalies or cardiac defects

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of extracranial anomalies (limb, cardiac, or facial dysmorphisms)
Positive genetic testing for FGFR or TWIST1 mutations
No premature suture fusion on imaging
History of positional preference without skull deformity progression

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (persistent vomiting, irritability, bulging fontanelle)
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniosynostosis: diagnosis, evaluation, and management. 2000.
Orphanet: Non-syndromic non-specific multisutural craniosynostosis. ORPHA:620158
Wilkie AO, et al. Craniosynostosis: genes and mechanisms. Hum Mol Genet. 2001.
